23:11.body: David asked whether Keilah would hand him over and whether Saul would come. Rashi and Ralbag learn that the Urim and Tumim answer only one question at a time, and Rashi adds they answer the one that should have come first.

sources.quote: שֶׁהַשּׁוֹאֵל שְׁנֵי דְבָרִים, אֵין מְשִׁיבִין לוֹ אֶלָּא אֶחָד, וְאֵין מְשִׁיבִין לוֹ אֶלָּא רִאשׁוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says one who asks two things is answered only one, and only the first, and David had asked out of order.

sources.quote: ולזה תמצא כי כששאל דוד על שתי שאלות לא באהו המענה כי אם באחת מהן
sources.says: Ralbag says that when David asked two questions, the answer came for only one of them.

sources.quote: השיבו לו על דבר שהיה מהראוי לשאול ראשון עליו, כי הירידה היא ראשון בזמן
sources.says: Metzudat David says they answered the matter he should have asked first, since Saul's coming down would happen first.

23:12.headline: A prediction that never happened, because David left
23:12.body: Keilah never handed David over, and Saul never came. Malbim says the answer was conditional: if David stayed, Saul would come and Keilah would give him up, and God told him so that he would leave.

sources.quote: כי דבר ה' היה אם לא ילך דוד משם ירד שאול והם יסגירו, שגלה לו דעת שאול ודעת אנשי קעילה, למען יזהר לצאת
sources.says: Malbim says God's word meant that if David did not leave, Saul would come and they would hand him over, revealing their intentions so that David would take care to leave.

23:16.headline: Jonathan 'strengthened his hand': a renewed pact, or courage
23:16.body: Rashi says Jonathan renewed the covenant between them. Radak says he gave David courage through God's promise, made by the prophet, that he would be king.

sources.quote: וַיְחַזֵּק אֶת יָדוֹ. חִדֵּשׁ בְּרִית שֶׁבֵּינֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says strengthening his hand means he renewed the covenant between them.

sources.quote: חזק ידו שלא יירא בדבר אלהים שהבטיחו על ידי הנביא כי ימלוך
sources.says: Radak says he strengthened David not to fear, by the word of God promised through the prophet that he would reign.

23:18.headline: 'Before God' means before the Urim and Tumim
23:18.body: Jonathan and David had already made a covenant, so why again? Metzudat David says this one was made before the Urim and Tumim, which the first was not, and Radak adds it may mean God as witness.

sources.quote: לפני האורים והתומים, כי הברית שמאז לא היה לפני ה׳
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means before the Urim and Tumim, since their earlier covenant was not before God.

sources.quote: אורים ותומים שהיו שם עם אביתר הכהן או פירו' שהאל יתברך יהיה עד בין שניהם
sources.says: Radak says it means the Urim and Tumim that were there with Abiathar the priest, or that God would be witness between them.

23:26.headline: Saul's men closed around David like a crown
23:26.body: עטרה means a crown. Rashi, Metzudat Zion and Radak say עטרים means surrounding him on every side, the way a crown circles the head.

sources.quote: מַקִּיפִים וְסוֹבְבִים מִצַּד אֶל צַד, כַּעֲטָרָה הַמַּקֶּפֶת אֶת הָרֹאשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says it means surrounding from side to side, like a crown that encircles the head.

sources.quote: מסבבים, כעטרה המסבבת את הראש
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means surrounding, like a crown around the head.

sources.quote: כמו סובבים כמו עטרה שהיא סובבת את הראש
sources.says: Radak says it means surrounding, like a crown that goes around the head.

23:27.headline: A messenger, or an angel, arrives just in time
23:27.body: Metzudat David says the מלאך was a human messenger, but Rashi says it was a real angel sent to save David. Radak cites a midrash where two sages argue for each view.

sources.quote: בא שליח אליו ללכת מול פלשתים
sources.says: Metzudat David says a messenger came telling Saul to go against the Philistines.

sources.quote: מַלְאָךְ מַמָּשׁ, כְּדֵי לְהַצִּיל אֶת דָּוִד
sources.says: Rashi says it was an actual angel, to save David.

sources.quote: א״ר יודן מלאך שליח היה אמר לו רבי פנחס וכי השליח יועץ הוא שהיה אומר מהרה ולכה אלא מלאך מן השמים היה
sources.says: Radak cites the midrash: Rabbi Yudan says it was a human messenger, and Rabbi Pinchas says a messenger would not give advice like 'hurry and go', so it was an angel from heaven.

25:3.headline: Nabal, 'fool': a nickname, not the name his parents gave
25:3.body: Radak's father said this was not the name his parents gave him. People called him נבל, a base fool, because he was so mean, and Malbim says each name in the verse fit its owner's deeds.

sources.quote: כי נבל זה לא היה שמו שקראו לו אבותיו אלא מרוב גריעות היו קוראין אותו בני אדם נבל
sources.says: Radak cites his father: Nabal was not the name his parents gave him, but people called him Nabal because he was so base.

sources.quote: וספר כי כשמם כן היו מעשיהם
sources.says: Malbim says their deeds matched their names.

25:3.headline: Calebite, 'as his heart', or dog-like?
25:3.body: The text is read כלבי, of Caleb's clan, as Rashi and the Targum say. Radak notes the written form כלבו can mean 'as his heart', bad inside and out, and Ralbag hears כלב, dog, snarling at others over food.

sources.quote: וְהוּא כָלִבִּי. מִבֵּית כָּלֵב
sources.says: Rashi says he was from the house of Caleb.

sources.quote: ואפשר לפרש הכ"ף לשמוש כפי הכתיב ר"ל כן היה מראה מעשיו רעים כמו שהיה לבו רע
sources.says: Radak says that by the written form one can read 'as his heart': his deeds were as bad as his heart, and he also links the word to a dog for his base deeds.

sources.quote: שלרוב אכזריותו היה תכונתו בתכונת הכלבים ששונאים בני מינם וינבחו להם
sources.says: Ralbag says that in his cruelty he was like dogs, which hate their own kind and bark at them, a sign of his stinginess.

25:3.headline: Abigail 'good of sense': wise, or good-looking?
25:3.body: The Targum and Radak read טובת שכל as wise and understanding. Radak also cites others who read it as if it said 'good in appearance'.

sources.quote: טובת שכל. כתרגומו חכימת מדע וי"מ שכל ענין עיון והבנה כאילו אמר טובת מראה
sources.says: Radak follows the Targum, wise in knowledge, and cites others who read it as if it said 'good of appearance'.

25:6.headline: A puzzling greeting: 'to life', 'next year', or 'to the rich'?
25:6.body: Rashi and Ralbag read כה לחי as 'so may it be next year', since חי can mean the coming season. Radak reads it as 'all your life', and cites others who read it as a greeting 'to the rich man'.

sources.quote: כֹּה יִהְיֶה לְשָׁנָה הַבָּאָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means: so may it be next year.

sources.quote: וקרא חי העתה העומד כמו שבארנו בדברי התורה על אמרו שוב אשוב אליך כעת חיה
sources.says: Ralbag says חי means the coming season, as in 'I will return to you at this season'.

sources.quote: כזה הטוב יהיה לך כל ימי חייך וכן תירגם יונתן כדין לחייך וי"מ ואמרתם כה לעשיר
sources.says: Radak says it means 'may this good be yours all your life', and cites others who read it as 'say this to the rich man'.

25:8.headline: Which 'good day': the shearing feast, or the eve of Rosh Hashanah?
25:8.body: Rashi and Radak say the shearing was a feast day, so David's men came when food was plentiful. Rashi also cites another view, that it was the eve of Rosh Hashanah and they needed food for the festival.

sources.quote: כי מנהגם לעשות משתה ויום טוב בעת שהיו גוזזים
sources.says: Radak says it was their custom to hold a feast and holiday at shearing time.

sources.quote: דָּבָר אַחֵר: עֶרֶב רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה הָיָה, וּצְרִיכִין אָנוּ לִסְעוּדַת יוֹם טוֹב
sources.says: Rashi gives another reading: it was the eve of Rosh Hashanah, and they needed food for the festival meal.

25:9.headline: 'They rested': tired from the road, or fell silent?
25:9.body: Rashi first reads it as resting from the journey only after they had spoken. The Targum, and Maimonides in the Guide, read it as falling silent to wait for Nabal's answer, having added nothing to provoke him.

sources.quote: יְגֵעִים הָיוּ מִטֹּרַח הַדֶּרֶךְ
sources.says: Rashi says they were tired from the road but did not rest until they had spoken, and gives the Targum's reading, that they stopped talking to hear his answer.

sources.quote: פירושו לדעתי: ופסקו מלדבר כדי לשמוע את התשובה
sources.says: The Guide says it means they stopped speaking to hear the answer, since no tiredness was mentioned.

sources.quote: בִּשְׁמָא דְדָוִד וּפְסָקוּ
sources.says: The Targum says they spoke in David's name and stopped.

25:13.headline: David girds his sword last, like the senior judge
25:13.body: Rashi cites the Talmud: in a capital case the junior judges speak first. Radak explains that David's men judged Nabal a rebel against the king, and David gave his view last so as not to sway them.

sources.quote: מִכָּאן שֶׁמַּתְחִילִין בְּדִינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת מִן הַקְּטַנִּים
sources.says: Rashi says this teaches that capital cases begin with the junior judges.

sources.quote: שאם היה הוא אומר דעתו בראשונה האחרים לא היו רוצים לחלוק עליו
sources.says: Radak says that had David spoken first, the others would not have wanted to disagree with him.

25:14.headline: Nabal swooped on them like a bird of prey
25:14.body: Rashi and Radak link ויעט to עיט, a bird of prey, and read it as driving the men off with harsh words. Ralbag says Nabal treated them the way that cruel bird does.

sources.quote: וּפֵירוּשׁוֹ הִכְרִיחָם בִּדְבָרָיו הָרָעִים), לְשׁוֹן עַיִט
sources.says: Rashi says he chased them off with his harsh words, and that the word comes from עיט, a bird of prey.

sources.quote: גער בהם והוא מענין עיט ומשרשו
sources.says: Radak says he scolded them, and the word comes from עיט and shares its root.

sources.quote: נהג בהם מנהג העיט והוא העוף הדורס שמתנהג באכזריות
sources.says: Ralbag says he behaved toward them like the עיט, the bird of prey that acts cruelly.

25:17.headline: בליעל: wicked, or stingy?
25:17.body: Metzudat Zion reads בליעל as a wicked man without the yoke of God. Ralbag says the word covers both the wicked and the stingy, and here it means stingy, as in Job 34:18.

sources.quote: איש רשע, בלי עול מקום
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a wicked man, without the yoke of God.

sources.quote: הנה בליעל נאמר בשתוף על הרשע ועל הכילי ומזה הענין הב' הוא בזה המקום
sources.says: Ralbag says בליעל is used for both the wicked and the miser, and here it has the second sense.

25:18.headline: Five 'made' sheep: cooked, or stuffed?
25:18.body: Radak and Metzudat Zion read עשויות as prepared and cooked. Rashi, from a Targum reading, says they were stuffed with minced meat and eggs, as Rabbi Kalonymus of Rome explained it.

sources.quote: ופירוש מתוקנות ומבושלות כמו וימהר לעשות אותו
sources.says: Radak says it means prepared and cooked, as in Abraham hurrying to prepare the calf.

sources.quote: מְמֻלָּאוֹת בָּשָׂר דַּק וּבֵיצִים
sources.says: Rashi says the Targum's word means stuffed with minced meat and eggs.

sources.quote: מתוקנות ומבושלות, כמו (בראשית יח ז)
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means prepared and cooked.

25:22.headline: 'One who urinates against a wall': every male, or even a dog?
25:22.body: Metzudat David says the phrase means every male. Rashi and Radak cite the sages, 'even a dog', and also the Targum's gentler reading, 'one who has knowledge', any thinking person.

sources.quote: כן יקרא הזכר, כי עושה קלוח למרחוק
sources.says: Metzudat David says this is a name for a male.

sources.quote: דָּבָר אַחֵר, אֲפִילוּ כֶּלֶב, שֶׁדַּרְכּוֹ לְהַשְׁתִּין בַּקִּיר
sources.says: Rashi gives the Targum's 'one who knows', and another reading: even a dog, which urinates against walls.

sources.quote: וי"ת ידע מדע ר"ל משית בקירות לבו כלומר בן דעת
sources.says: Radak says the Targum reads it as one who has knowledge, who reflects in the walls of his heart.

25:22.headline: David's oath falls on 'David's enemies', not on David
25:22.body: David swears God should punish him if he spares Nabal's house, but the verse says 'David's enemies'. Radak calls this a polite cover for David himself, and Metzudat David says the text softened it because David later took the oath back.

sources.quote: לאויבי דוד. כנוי הוא לדוד
sources.says: Radak says 'David's enemies' is a polite way of saying David.

sources.quote: ולפי שבסוף חזר בו, לזה כינה הכתוב ואמר לאויבי דוד
sources.says: Metzudat David says that because David took it back in the end, the text softened it to 'David's enemies'.

25:29.headline: 'Bound in the bundle of life': the soul after death
25:29.body: Maimonides cites this verse in the Guide for the meaning of נפש that is left of a person after death. The Targum and Ralbag likewise read 'the bundle of life' as the life of the world to come.

sources.quote: והוא שם הדבר הנשאר מן האדם לאחר המוות
sources.says: The Guide says one meaning of נפש is what remains of a person after death, and cites this verse.

sources.quote: הוא העולם הבא כי שם תתאחד הנפש במושכליה
sources.says: Ralbag says the bundle of life is the world to come.

sources.quote: גְנִיזָא בִּגְנַז חַיֵי עַלְמָא
sources.says: The Targum says the soul will be stored in the treasury of eternal life.

25:29.headline: The enemies' souls flung about like a sling stone
25:29.body: Radak cites Rabbi Eliezer: the souls of the righteous are stored under God's throne, while the souls of the wicked are flung from one end of the world to the other with no rest. Metzudat David reads it the same way.

sources.quote: ונשמתן של רשעים מטרפות ומשוטטות מסוף העולם ועד סופו ואין להם מנוחה
sources.says: Radak cites the sages that the souls of the wicked are tossed and wander from one end of the world to the other with no rest.

sources.quote: תהיה משוטטת נעה ונדה, כהאבן הקלוע בכף הקלע
sources.says: Metzudat David says the soul will wander back and forth like a stone in a sling.

25:32.headline: A letter missing from Abigail's name
25:32.body: Here her name is spelled without one letter, אביגל. Radak says names often vary, but cites a midrash: when she said 'remember your maidservant' she offered herself, and the text cut her name short.

sources.quote: ויש בו דרש כי כשאמרה וזכרת את אמתך פקרה עצמה לו וכיון שפקרה עצמה לו פגמה הכתוב בקריאה
sources.says: Radak says the short spelling is a common variant, and cites a midrash that because she offered herself to David, the text marred her name.

25:37.headline: 'His heart died', yet he lived ten more days
25:37.body: Maimonides says in the Guide that 'death' here means a grave illness. Metzudat David reads it as an overstatement for great fear, and Rashi says Nabal was crushed by grief over the gift.

sources.quote: ושמה של המחלה הקשה
sources.says: The Guide says מות also names a severe illness, and that this verse means Nabal's grave sickness.

sources.quote: אמר על דרך גוזמא והפלגה, על גודל החרדה מפחד דוד
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is an overstatement for his great fear of David.

sources.quote: שֶׁנִּצְטַעֵר עַל הַמִּנְחָה שֶׁהוּבְאָת לְדָוִד
sources.says: Rashi says he was pained over the gift brought to David.

25:38.headline: Why Nabal died after ten days
25:38.body: Rashi says God waited out the seven days of mourning for Samuel, then Nabal was sick three days and died. Others say they were the ten days of repentance, but Radak objects that a man whose heart had turned to stone could not repent.

sources.quote: שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי אֶבְלוֹ שֶׁל שְׁמוּאֵל תָּלָה לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says God held off for the seven days of mourning for Samuel, so the mourning for a wicked man would not mix with it, and also cites the ten days of repentance.

sources.quote: והם עשרה ימים הידועים של תשובה שבין ר"ה ליוהכ"פ
sources.says: Malbim cites the sages that these are the ten days of repentance between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur.

sources.quote: ואני אומר כי לרעתו היו אלה העשרה ימים לא לטובתו
sources.says: Radak says the ten days were for his harm, not his good, since a man whose heart was like stone could not repent.

26:5.headline: The camp is called a 'circle'
26:5.body: Radak and Metzudat Zion say an army camp is called מעגל, from עגול, circle, because troops camped in a ring. Ralbag says the ring let them see anyone coming from any side.

sources.quote: מקום המחנה יקרא מעגל לפי שחונים שם העם בסבוב
sources.says: Radak says the camp is called מעגל because the people camp there in a ring.

sources.quote: דרך המחנה לחנות בעגול, למען יראו מסביב כל הבא עליהם
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says a camp is pitched in a circle so they can see anyone coming at them from all around.

sources.quote: והוא היה בדמות עגול למען יראו הבאים אליהם מכל הצדדים
sources.says: Ralbag says the camp was round so they could see anyone approaching from every side.

26:12.headline: David took the spear himself, not trusting Abishai
26:12.body: David had told Abishai to take the spear, but the verse says David took it. Radak and Metzudat David say he changed his mind, afraid Abishai could not hold back from striking Saul.

sources.quote: נתחרט בו ולא רצה שיקרב אבישי אליו שמא לא יוכל לכבוש את יצרו ויכנו
sources.says: Radak says David regretted his words and did not want Abishai near Saul, in case he could not control himself and struck him.

sources.quote: חזר דוד לקחתו בעצמו, כי לא האמין לאבישי פן יכה עמו נפש שאול
sources.says: Metzudat David says David went back and took it himself, because he did not trust Abishai not to kill Saul with it.

26:19.headline: David said God 'incited' Saul, and was later incited himself
26:19.body: Rashi reads it as stirring Saul to hate him. Radak cites the sages: because David used the word 'incite' of God, he later stumbled through incitement, as in 'He incited David against them' in the census story.

sources.quote: לִשְׂנָאָתִי, כָּל הֲסָתָה לְשׁוֹן שׂוּמָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means stirred you to hate me, and that every incitement means setting something in someone's mind.

sources.quote: ורז"ל דרשו כי בעון שאמר לשון הסתה על הבורא ית' חטא בהסתה ויסת את דוד בהם
sources.says: Radak cites the sages that because he spoke of God inciting, he sinned through incitement, as it says 'He incited David against them'.

26:19.headline: 'Let Him smell an offering'
26:19.body: Radak and Metzudat Zion read ירח from ריח, smell: if God stirred Saul against me, let Him smell my offering and be appeased. Rashi reads it as 'may He accept my prayer with mercy'.

sources.quote: ירח. מלשון ריח
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says ירח comes from ריח, smell.

sources.quote: כלומר אקריב לפניו מנחה שיריחה וירצה בה לכפר עוני
sources.says: Radak says it means: I will bring Him an offering that He will smell and accept, to atone for my sin.

sources.quote: יְקַבֵּל בְּרַחֲמִים תְּפִלָּתִי
sources.says: Rashi says it means: may He accept my prayer with mercy.

26:20.headline: The hunted 'caller' bird, and David calling from the hill
26:20.body: Rashi and Metzudat David say the קורא is a bird that is hunted in the hills. Malbim hears a play: David himself is 'the caller', since he has just shouted to Saul's camp from a hilltop.

sources.quote: עוֹף שֶׁשְּׁמוֹ קוֹרֵא
sources.says: Rashi says it is a bird named קורא.

sources.quote: והוא שם עוף אשר יתענגו המלכים לרדוף אחריו ולצודו
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is a bird that kings enjoy chasing and hunting.

sources.quote: אמר על עצמו שם הקורא בהרים שעומד בהרים וקורא מרחוק כמו שעשה עתה
sources.says: Malbim says David called himself 'the caller in the hills', one who stands on the hills and calls from afar, as he had just done.

26:25.headline: Saul's blessing: the Targum hears 'you will reign'
26:25.body: Saul says David 'will surely do and surely succeed'. The Targum renders it 'you will surely reign and surely succeed', and Metzudat David reads it as doing wondrous deeds.

sources.quote: אַף מִמְלַךְ תִּמְלוֹךְ וְאַף אַצְלַח תַּצְלַח
sources.says: The Targum says: you will surely reign and surely succeed.

sources.quote: וגם עשה תעשה מעשים נפלאים, וגם תצליח בהם
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means you will do wondrous deeds and succeed in them.

30:6.headline: Something "pressed" on David: the disaster itself
30:6.body: ותצר is a feminine verb with no named subject. Radak says it comes from the word for distress, and the subject is this disaster, which pressed hard on David.

sources.quote: ותצר לדוד. שרשו יצר והוא מענין צרה וצוקה ובאמרו לשון נקבה ר"ל זאת הרעה
sources.says: Radak says the root is יצר, meaning trouble and distress, and the feminine form refers to this disaster.

30:8.headline: "Shall I chase them?" or "I will chase them"?
30:8.body: ארדף has no Hebrew question marker. Metzudat Zion and Radak say it is still a question, shall I pursue; Malbim reads it as a statement, I will pursue anyway, and the only question is whether he will catch them.

sources.quote: תחסר ה״א השאלה, ומשפטו: הארדוף
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the question letter ה is missing, and it should read shall I pursue.

sources.quote: ארדף. דרך שאלה בלא ה"א השאלה
sources.says: Radak says it is a question without the question letter.

sources.quote: ארדוף רצה לומר אני ארדוף בכל אופן ושאלתי הוא האשיגנו
sources.says: Malbim says it means I will pursue in any case, and my question is whether I will overtake them.

30:12.headline: Raisins: grapes named for drying up
30:12.body: צמקים are dried grapes; Metzudat David says two clusters of them. Metzudat Zion links the word to Hosea's ושדים צומקים, breasts that have dried up.

sources.quote: צמוקים. ענבים יבשים, והוא מלשון (הושע ט יד): ושדים צומקים
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says they are dried grapes, from the word in Hosea for dried-up breasts.

sources.quote: שני אשכלות צמוקים
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means two clusters of raisins.

30:16.headline: Spread out everywhere, like the quail around the camp
30:16.body: נטשים means scattered. Metzudat Zion compares the quail spread over Israel's camp, and Malbim says the raiders lay spread out with no guards, sure that no enemy was coming.

sources.quote: נטושים. מפוזרים, כמו (במדבר יא לא): ויטוש על המחנה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means scattered, as in the verse where the quail spread over the camp.

sources.quote: שהיו נטושים לא כגדוד בעת שעדיין מורא האויב עליהם שעומדים ביחד ומעמידים שומרים סביב
sources.says: Malbim says they were spread out, not like a troop still afraid of an enemy, which stays together and posts guards.

30:18.headline: Why the verse names David twice
30:18.body: The verse could simply have said he rescued his two wives. Malbim says the name David is repeated to show he saved his wives with his own hands, while the rest were saved through his men.

sources.quote: לכן כפל השם שנית הציל דוד רצה לומר בעצמו, כי יתר העם הציל באמצעות אנשיו
sources.says: Malbim says the name is repeated to mean David rescued them himself, while the rest of the people he rescued through his men.

5:4.headline: Dagon was half fish, so only the fish part was left
5:4.body: The name דגון sounds like דג, fish. Radak says the idol was a fish from the waist down. When its head and hands broke off, "only Dagon was left" means only the fish body.

sources.quote: אמרו כי דגון מטבורו ולמטה היה צורת דג לפיכך נקרא דגון
sources.says: Radak reports that Dagon had the shape of a fish from the navel down, and that is why it was called Dagon.

sources.quote: רק דגון נשאר עליו צורת דג נשאר עליו
sources.says: Radak explains "only Dagon remained" as "only the fish shape remained".

sources.quote: אצל דגון.} דמות עשוי כדמות דג
sources.says: Rashi says Dagon was an image made in the shape of a fish.

5:8.headline: "Let it go around to Gath": why the far city?
5:8.body: Metzudat Zion reads יסב simply as "let it be brought". Malbim hears "go the long way around". The lords chose far-off Gath because they thought the sickness was a natural one that spreads only nearby.

sources.quote: יסוב.} רצה לומר יובא
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says יסוב means "let it be brought".

sources.quote: ולא שלחוהו לעיר קרובה לאשדוד רק לגת שהיה רחוק
sources.says: Malbim says they did not send it to a city near Ashdod but to Gath, which was far away.

5:9.headline: Written with shin, read as "hidden": the sores were inside
5:9.body: וישתרו is spelled with ש but read as if it were ס, from סתר, hidden. So in Gath the sores were inside the body, which made them worse.

sources.quote: כמו ויסתרו, שהרי הוא במסורת כתובים שי״ן, ומפרשים בלשון סמ״ך
sources.says: Rashi says it is like ויסתרו: the tradition lists it as written with shin and explained as samekh.

sources.quote: ופי' שהיה להם מכת הטחורים במקום סתר מבפנים
sources.says: Radak says it means the sores were in a hidden place inside them.

5:11.headline: Rashi says every "panic" in the Bible comes from thunder
5:11.body: מהומה means panic or uproar. Rashi cites an old rule that every מהומה is caused by thunder, learned from a verse two chapters later.

sources.quote: כל מהומות על ידי רעם, וזה אביהן
sources.says: Rashi says every מהומה comes through thunder, and that the model case is God thundering on the Philistines in I Samuel 7:10.

6:3.headline: Why 'return' a guilt offering they never took?
6:3.body: The priests say השב תשיבו, 'you must return' a guilt offering. Malbim asks how you return something you never took. His answer: the plague took the shape of their sin, so they hand that shape back to God, in gold.

sources.quote: שלשון השבה לא יצדק רק אם משיב הדבר בעצמו שבו אשם
sources.says: Malbim says the word 'return' only fits when someone gives back the very thing he wronged with.

sources.quote: ואם תשיבו הצורה הזאת המשחתת אל הקדושה, ובה תכבדוהו תחת אשר בה מריתם
sources.says: Malbim says they return the shape of the plague to holiness, honoring God with the thing they sinned with.

sources.quote: הֶכֵּר דָּבָר שֶׁאַתֶּם מוֹדִים שֶׁמְּעַלְתֶּם בּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the guilt offering is a sign that they admit they wronged the ark.

6:5.headline: Maimonides on צלם: shape, or what a thing is for
6:5.body: צלם is the word in 'God made man in His image'. Maimonides uses this verse to argue it need not mean outward shape. The golden 'images of your swellings' mattered for their purpose, to drive the plague away, not for their look.

sources.quote: כי המבוקש מהם היה עניין הרחקת פגע הטחורים, לא תבנית הטחורים
sources.says: Maimonides says these images were wanted for removing the plague of swellings, not for the shape of the swellings.

sources.quote: יהיה "צלם" מונח רב־משמעי או מסופק
sources.says: He adds that if the word here does mean outward shape, then צלם is a word with more than one meaning.

6:7.headline: Not cows that 'go up' but cows still nursing
6:7.body: עלות looks like the verb for going up. Rashi says it means nursing. Radak says the cows are named after their young, called עוללים, sucklings.

sources.quote: עָלוֹת. מְנִיקוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says עלות means nursing.

sources.quote: ונקראו עלות על שם היונקים שנקראו עולים ועוללים
sources.says: Radak says they are called עלות after the sucklings, who are called עולים and עוללים.

6:12.headline: The cows went straight, or they sang
6:12.body: Plainly, וישרנה means the cows went straight. The sages heard שירה, song: the cows sang as they carried the ark. Rashi also notes the word mixes a male and a female verb form.

sources.quote: הֲרֵי תֵּבָה זוֹ אַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס
sources.says: Rashi says this word is both male and female in form.

sources.quote: אוֹמְרִים שִׁירָה: רֹנִּי רֹנִּי הַשִּׁטָּה
sources.says: Rashi brings the Talmud's teaching that they sang a song, 'Sing, sing, O acacia'.

sources.quote: וּלְפִי פְשׁוּטוֹ, ׳וַיִּשַּׁרְנָה׳, לְשׁוֹן ׳יְשַׁר דֶּרֶךְ׳
sources.says: Rashi says that in its plain sense the word means going straight.

sources.quote: ובדרש שאמרו שירה הוציאו וישרנה מלשון שירה
sources.says: Radak says the midrash that they sang took וישרנה from the word for song.

6:18.headline: The great stone is renamed 'mourning'
6:18.body: The verse says אבל, mourning, where we expect אבן, stone. Rashi says a lamed took the place of the nun. The stone got the name because the people mourned there after the deaths that follow.

sources.quote: הִיא הָאֶבֶן הַגְּדוֹלָה הָאֲמוּרָה לְמַעְלָה, שֶׁהַלָּמֶ״ד בָּאָה בִּמְקוֹם נוּ״ן
sources.says: Rashi says it is the great stone mentioned above, with lamed in place of nun.

sources.quote: וּמִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵרַע לָהֶם אֲבֵלוּת בַּדָּבָר, קְרָאָהּ אָבֵל
sources.says: Rashi says it is called mourning because mourning came upon them through it.

sources.quote: ונקראת האבן הגדולה אבל על האבל שנעשה בו כמו שאמר ויתאבלו העם
sources.says: Radak says the great stone was called mourning for the mourning held there, as the next verse says.

6:19.headline: Seventy men, fifty thousand men: which was it?
6:19.body: The verse gives two numbers side by side. The Aramaic translation splits them: seventy elders and fifty thousand of the people. The sages read it as seventy men, each worth fifty thousand.

sources.quote: וּקְטַל בְּסָבֵי עַמָא שַׁבְעִין גַבְרָא וּבִקְהָלָא חַמְשִׁין אַלְפֵי גַבְרָא
sources.says: The Aramaic translation says He killed seventy of the elders and fifty thousand of the congregation.

sources.quote: שִׁבְעִים אִישׁ, שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד הָיָה שָׁקוּל כַּחֲמִשִּׁים אֶלֶף
sources.says: Rashi brings the sages: seventy men, each one equal to fifty thousand.

sources.quote: חסר וי"ו השמוש וחמשים אלף איש
sources.says: Radak says the word 'and' is missing, so it means seventy men and fifty thousand men.

9:1.headline: Aviel was also called Ner, 'lamp', for lighting dark alleys
9:1.body: Chronicles calls Kish's father Ner, while here he is Aviel. Radak cites Vayikra Rabbah: his real name was Aviel, but people called him Ner because he lit lamps in dark alleys for others.

sources.quote: ומצאתי בויקרא רבה כי עיקר שמו אביאל והיו קוראים שמו נר לפי שהיה מדליק נרות במבואות האפלות
sources.says: Radak cites Vayikra Rabbah that his main name was Aviel, and he was called Ner because he lit lamps in dark alleys.

sources.quote: שלאביאל היו קורים לו נר על שהיה מדליק נרות לרבים במבואות האפלות
sources.says: Malbim cites the sages that Aviel was called Ner because he lit lamps for the public in dark alleys, a sign of his good character.

9:2.headline: 'Good': handsome, or good in character?
9:2.body: Radak and the Targum read טוב as good-looking. Malbim reads it as good character: though young and hot-blooded, Saul was good toward God and people.

sources.quote: פי' טוב בתואר ובמראה וכת"י עולים ושפיר
sources.says: Radak says good means good in form and looks, and the Targum renders it 'young and handsome'.

sources.quote: הגם שהיה בחור בשנים ורתיחת דמו לא שקטה בכ"ז היה טוב עם אלהים ואדם
sources.says: Malbim says that though he was young and his blood still hot, he was good toward God and people.

sources.quote: נבחר במעשיו ויפה מראה
sources.says: Metzudat David reads both senses: chosen in his deeds and handsome.

9:3.headline: The donkeys were not really lost, only hidden for a while
9:3.body: Malbim notes that 'lost' normally takes the word 'from', but here the donkeys are lost 'to Kish'. He says they were only hidden for a time, so Saul would be sent to look and would reach Samuel.

sources.quote: והנה פעל אבד נקשר תמיד עם מם ופה בא בלמ"ד, כי לא נאבדו באמת רק נעלמו בשעתם
sources.says: Malbim says the verb 'lose' always goes with 'from', but here with 'to', because the donkeys were not truly lost, only hidden for the time.

9:5.headline: Zuph: the land of the 'watcher', the prophet
9:5.body: Rashi follows the Targum, 'the land where the prophet is', and says צוף is like צופה, a watcher or seer. Ralbag says the area was named after Zuph, an ancestor of Samuel's family.

sources.quote: צוּף. כְּמוֹ ׳צוֹפֶה׳
sources.says: Rashi says צוף is like צופה, one who watches.

sources.quote: בְּאַרְעָא דְבָּהּ נְבִיָא דַייָ
sources.says: The Targum renders it 'the land where the prophet of the Lord is'.

sources.quote: וקראה ארץ צוף לפי שהיו היושבים שם מתיחסים בצוף
sources.says: Ralbag says it was called the land of Zuph because the people living there traced their family to Zuph.

9:7.headline: Not 'prophet' here: נביא means 'what shall we bring'
9:7.body: The same letters spell נביא, prophet, two verses later. Here Metzudat Zion says it comes from bringing, and Rashi says Saul did not know Samuel and thought he would ask a fee.

sources.quote: נביא. מלשון הבאה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word here comes from bringing.

sources.quote: לֹא הָיָה שָׁאוּל מַכִּיר בְּמַעֲשָׂיו שֶׁל שְׁמוּאֵל, וְסָבַר שֶׁיִּשְׁאַל שָׂכָר
sources.says: Rashi says Saul did not know Samuel's ways and thought he would ask for payment.

9:7.headline: A gift for seeing a great man's face
9:7.body: Rashi brings two readings of this word. The Targum takes it as 'something fitting', and Menachem as a gift for being received by a king, from אשורנו, 'I behold him'.

sources.quote: וּמְנַחֵם פֵּירַשׁ: ׳תְּשׁוּרָה׳, לְשׁוֹן תִּקְרֹבֶת, רְאוֹת פְּנֵי מֶלֶךְ וְאָדָם חָשׁוּב
sources.says: Rashi gives the Targum's 'something fitting', then Menachem's reading, a present for seeing the face of a king or important person, from 'I behold him', and says Menachem's words seem right.

sources.quote: ותשורה. דורון, כמו (ישעיהו נז ט): ותשורי למלך בשמן
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a gift, as in Isaiah 57:9.

9:9.headline: Seer and prophet: one sees, the other speaks
9:9.body: Radak says נביא comes from speech, as in ניב שפתים, 'fruit of the lips', while a רואה sees the future in a vision. Malbim adds that people asked the seer about private things like lost animals, while the prophet spoke to the whole nation.

sources.quote: לפי שלשון נביא הוא לשון דבור מענין ניב שפתים
sources.says: Radak says נביא is a word of speech, related to 'fruit of the lips', and a seer is one who sees in prophetic vision.

sources.quote: שהנביא נקרא שמו על שם דברותיו ותוכחותיו (מלשון ניב שפתים)
sources.says: Malbim says the prophet is named for his speeches and rebukes, while the seer is named for seeing private matters by the holy spirit.

sources.quote: לְמִי שֶׁקּוֹרִים אוֹתוֹ נָבִיא הַיּוֹם, הָיוּ קוֹרִים לְפָנִים ׳רוֹאֶה׳
sources.says: Rashi says the one called a prophet today was once called a seer.

9:12.headline: 'He is here': a midrash sees a cloud over Samuel's door
9:12.body: The girls answer with one word, יש, 'there is'. Radak cites a midrash that reads it as 'see the cloud tied over his door', linking it to a verse about the cloud in Numbers that also begins with יש.

sources.quote: יש בו דרש אמרו לו תראה הענן קשור על פתחו כד"א ויש אשר יהיה הענן
sources.says: Radak cites a midrash that they told him to look at the cloud tied over his door, as in 'and there was when the cloud would be'.

9:12.headline: The 'high place': an altar, or a dining hall?
9:12.body: The Targum calls every such במה a 'house of reclining', a dining hall. Rashi and Radak explain that after Shiloh was destroyed, local altars were allowed, and the townspeople ate their peace offerings together there.

sources.quote: כל במה בזה הענין ובדומה לו תרגם יונתן בית אסחרותא
sources.says: Radak says that every במה in this kind of story the Targum renders as a house of reclining, where the town ate its peace offerings.

sources.quote: מִשֶׁחָרְבָה שִׁילֹה הֻתְּרוּ הַבָּמוֹת, וְהָיוּ מַקְרִיבִין שְׁלָמִים בַּבָּמָה, וְאוֹכְלִים יַחַד
sources.says: Rashi says that once Shiloh was destroyed, local altars were allowed, and people offered peace offerings there and ate together.

9:13.headline: The blessing Samuel said before the sacrificial meal
9:13.body: The Targum says Samuel 'breaks the bread'. Rashi and Radak say a special blessing was said over peace offerings: 'who commanded us to eat the sacrifice'.

sources.quote: עַל הַשְּׁלָמִים מְבָרְכִין בַּאֲכִילָתָם
sources.says: Rashi says the Targum reads it as breaking bread, and that over peace offerings a blessing was said when eating them.

sources.quote: כי כשהיו אוכלין זבחי שלמים היו מברכים עליו אשר קדשנו במצוותיו וצוונו לאכול הזבח
sources.says: Radak says that when they ate peace offerings they blessed God who commanded them to eat the sacrifice.

9:17.headline: 'He will restrain my people': rule them, or hold back the enemy?
9:17.body: Rashi and Radak read יעצר as ruling: a king holds his people together in war and keeps them from evil. The Targum, as Radak notes, reads it as removing the Philistines' rule from Israel.

sources.quote: כָּךְ דֶּרֶךְ הַמּוֹשֵׁל, לַעֲצֹר הָעָם בַּמִּלְחָמָה
sources.says: Rashi says it means to rule, since a ruler holds the people together in war and holds each one back from doing evil.

sources.quote: ואמר יעצור כלומר שיעצור פלשתים וימנעם מלהלחם בישראל
sources.says: Radak says it can mean he will restrain the Philistines and stop them fighting Israel, as the Targum suggests.

sources.quote: דֵין יַעְדֵי מַרְוָתָא מִן עַמִי
sources.says: The Targum says this one will remove the rule of others from My people.

9:19.headline: 'I am the seer': the sages say Samuel slipped here
9:19.body: Radak says answering was not proud, since Saul asked him directly. But he cites the sages that it was a slip, and God answered it when Samuel misjudged Eliab: 'Did you not say, I am the seer?'

sources.quote: אמר לו הקדוש ברוך הוא אתה הוא הרואה אני מודיעך שאין אתה הרואה
sources.says: Radak cites the sages that God told Samuel: you are the seer? I will show you that you are not, which He did at David's anointing.

9:24.headline: 'The shank and what was on it', or the fat tail?
9:24.body: Rashi, Radak and the Targum read והעליה as 'what was on it', the thigh above the shank. Radak also cites the sages' dispute: one reads it as the fat tail, אליה, another as the breast.

sources.quote: אֶת הַשּׁוֹק וְהַיָּרֵךְ שֶׁעָלֶיהָ
sources.says: Rashi says it is the shank and the thigh on it.

sources.quote: ר' יוחנן אומר שוק ואליה ר' אליעזר אומר שוק וחזה
sources.says: Radak cites the sages: Rabbi Yochanan says the shank and the fat tail, Rabbi Eliezer says the shank and the breast.

9:26.headline: 'I will send you': give leave, or walk you out?
9:26.body: Metzudat Zion reads ואשלחך here as 'I will escort you', as Abraham walked his guests out in Genesis 18:16. In verse 19 he reads the same verb as giving leave, since a guest does not go without permission.

sources.quote: ואשלחך. אלוה אותך
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means 'I will accompany you'.

sources.quote: לפי שאין דרך ללכת בלא נטילת רשות
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says Samuel promised to send him because one does not leave without taking leave.
